command:
gh pr create --base main --title "APRV-382: log.advance is autonomous for the daemon actor alone" --body-file - <<'EOF'
Closes APRV-382.

Carter asked on 2026-09-19 whether a records advance should be autonomous. Three advances that day each stopped on the one-in-a-hundred live draw while he was away from the phone, and the tap decided nothing: an advance publishes records the log already holds, appends nothing and decides nothing, and CI's protected-path guard reads grants that exist whether or not an advance ran.

## The rule

The class grammar carries no actor condition, so this is written as two classes:

- `log.advance.daemon` — the daemon's own cadence advance, `autonomous` under the proposal page.
- `log.advance` — everybody else, untouched at `supervised-live 0.01`: a session in a worktree, the orchestrator's own `approval log advance --pr`, a human terminal.

Nothing an agent can type reaches the looser line, and that is structural rather than a check: `approval log advance` classifies `log.advance` whoever runs it (`approval hook classify` confirms), and the daemon's class is asked for only from inside the daemon process. Starting a daemon is `gate.self`, which this policy leaves at the fail-closed manual default.

The runtime carries the same rule a second time so a policy loosened past this decision does not quietly grant it: a cycle that is not the daemon's and whose class resolves `autonomous` is refused `advance-actor-not-daemon` before anything is appended.

## Who is running it

`src/core/daemon-actor.ts` holds one process fact. `markDaemonProcess()` takes no arguments and records `process.pid`; the `Daemon` constructor calls it, so `approval up`, `approval daemon run`, the shutdown flush and a `--once` tick are one actor. It is deliberately not a field on `AdvanceInput`: a field a caller sets is a self-reported field, and SPEC §11.1 invariant 4 says a self-reported field never reduces scrutiny.

Fallback: a daemon under a policy with no rule on the daemon class asks under `log.advance`, exactly as today. So the cadence in the primary checkout is unchanged between this merging and Carter applying the page; resolving to the manual default there would have been a phone tap per advance for a policy that had decided nothing.

## The pin that moved

`log.advance` was never in `REPO_POLICY_EXPECTATIONS` (APRV-296 removed it on purpose). What would have failed the amend on the laptop is the REACHABILITY check: `emittableClass` answers from the command classifier's table, and a class no command spells is refused `unreachable`, which is true of the classifier and false of the runtime. So `src/core/command-class.ts` gains `RUNTIME_CLASSES` (classes a runtime cycle asks the gate for directly) and `emittableClass` reads it. `CLASSIFIER_CLASSES` is untouched: `tests/cli-hook.test.ts` requires every member of it to have a row in `docs/claude-code-hook.md`, and the daemon class is not a hook row.

`tests/dogfood.test.ts` gains two pins. One is state-tolerant, and holds on both sides of the ceremony: `log.advance` is never `autonomous`, and any autonomy sits on the daemon's class. The other parses `docs/proposals/log-advance-daemon-2026-09.md`, applies it to the live `APPROVAL.md` bytes through the real `parseProposal`/`planApply`, loads the result and runs `checkPolicyExpectations` over it — the amend's own laptop check, in memory, with `APPROVAL.md` never written (the suite's `after` hook compares its bytes).

## The dry run

`approval policy apply --dry-run` could not be run from this session. The verb classifies `policy.core` and the hook denied it, as designed:

```
hook-class-human-only: class policy.core resolves to human-only (amended SPEC.md §5.2, APRV-185),
so this command may not run under an agent.
```

The dogfood test above is the same three steps the verb performs before it writes anything.

## No schema change, no SPEC change, no APPROVAL.md edit

`envelope.schema.json` constrains an action class by pattern rather than by enum, so `log.advance.daemon` validates as it stands.

## What Carter runs

After this merges:

```bash
cd /Users/carter/dev/approval-md && approval log sync && npm ci && npm run build
cd /Users/carter/dev/approval-md && approval policy apply docs/proposals/log-advance-daemon-2026-09.md
```

`--pr` is the default since APRV-360, so no flag. Then restart the daemon (`approval up`) so the cadence runs on the build that knows the new class.

## Tests

`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`: clean. `npm test` after `npm ci`: 4735 pass, 45 fail, exit 1. Every failure is in `tests/adapter-email.test.ts`, `tests/smtp-probe.test.ts` and the four `setup adapter email` cases of `tests/cli-setup.test.ts`: the pre-existing local SMTP failures on Node v26. CI on Node 22 is the truth here.

New coverage: five cases in `tests/daemon-advance-actor.test.ts` (the route over loaded policies both ways; the daemon advancing unasked under `log.advance.daemon` with `log.advance` left at `manual`, read back off the log; the fallback gating under `log.advance`; a non-daemon actor refused `advance-actor-not-daemon` with the record count unmoved), all through the real append path over a real git topology with `gh` stubbed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
